title: Check if Two Strings are Permutations
source: Classic warm-up hashing problem (anagram / permutation check)
statement:
You are given two strings `S` and `T` consisting of lowercase English letters.

`T` is a **permutation** of `S` if `T` can be obtained by rearranging the characters of `S` — that is, both strings contain **exactly the same characters with exactly the same counts** (so they also have the same length).

Print `YES` if `T` is a permutation of `S`, otherwise print `NO`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the string `S`.
The second line contains the string `T`.
constraints:
- `1 ≤ |S|, |T| ≤ 10^5`
- `S` and `T` contain only lowercase letters `a-z`
- `|S|` and `|T|` may be different

samples.explanation: Both strings contain `e, i, l, n, s, t` once each.
Same length and same set of letters, but `S` has two `a`s while `T` has only one.
Different lengths can never be permutations of each other.

hints: If the lengths differ, the answer is immediately `NO`.
Comparing `sorted(S) == sorted(T)` works in O(N log N). Can you do it in O(N)?
Use a count array of size 26: add 1 for each character of `S`, subtract 1 for each character of `T`. The answer is `YES` iff every entry ends at 0.
editorial:
### Intuition
Two strings are permutations of each other exactly when their **character frequency tables** are identical.

### Approach 1 — Sorting
`sorted(S) == sorted(T)`. Simple and correct, **O(N log N)**.

### Approach 2 — Counting (optimal)
1. If `len(S) != len(T)`, print `NO`.
2. Keep `cnt[26]`. For every `c` in `S` do `cnt[c] += 1`; for every `c` in `T` do `cnt[c] -= 1`.
3. Print `YES` iff all counts are zero.

`collections.Counter(S) == Counter(T)` is the same idea in one line.

**O(N)** time, **O(1)** extra space (26 counters).

### Common mistakes
- Checking only that both strings use the *same set* of letters (`set(S) == set(T)`) — ignores counts (sample 2).
- Skipping the length check when using a one-sided count (only checking that each char of `T` exists in `S`).
- Printing `Yes`/`yes` instead of exactly `YES`.
